name: LAUGAVATNSMANNI
description: Laugavatnsmanni is a popular Icelandic trick-taking game for three players, part of the 'Manni' family of games (Manni means 'little man' or 'chap'). Played over 18 rounds, each player must declare one of six different contracts in each rotation, aiming for specific trick targets. The game is unique for its use of a 4-card 'Manni' (dummy) pile that players can use to improve their hands before the round begins.

content.text: Laugavatnsmanni is a popular Icelandic trick-taking game for three players, part of the 'Manni' family of games (Manni means 'little man' or 'chap'). Played over 18 rounds, each player must declare one of six different contracts in each rotation, aiming for specific trick targets. The game is unique for its use of a 4-card 'Manni' (dummy) pile that players can use to improve their hands before the round begins.
Developed in the mid-20th century in the Laugavatn region of Iceland. It is a refinement of older Icelandic 'Vista' and 'Manni' games, standardized for school and social club competitive play.
48 cards (remove all four 2s from a standard 52-card deck). Ace is high in all contracts EXCEPT Nullo.
Each player is dealt 16 cards in packets of 4. The remaining 4 cards form the 'Manni' pile, placed face-down in the center.
